source_text: ΤΟΥ ΕΝ ΑΓΙΟΙΣ ΠΑΤΡΟΣ ΗΜΩΝ ΑΘΑΝΑΣΙΟΥ, ΑΡΧΙΕΠΙΣΚΟΠΟΥ ΑΛΕΞΑΝΔΡΕΙΑΣ, ΕΠΙΣΤΟΛΗ ΠΡΟΣ ΑΔΕΛΦΙΟΝ ΕΠΙΣΚΟΠΟΝ ΚΑΙ ΟΜΟΛΟΓΗΤΗΝ, ΚΑΤΑ ΑΡΕΙΑΝΩΝ. Ἐντυχόντες τοῖς παρὰ τῆς σῆς θεοσεβείας γραφεῖσι, τὴν μὲν σὴν εἰς Χριστὸν εὐσέβειαν ἀληθῶς ἀπεδεξάμεθα, καὶ τὸν μὲν Θεὸν προηγουμένως ἐδοξάσαμεν, δεδωκότα σοι τὴν τοιαύτην χάριν, ὥστε καὶ τὴν φρόνησιν ἔχειν ὀρθὴν, καὶ μὴ ἀγνοεῖν κατὰ τὸ δυνατὸν τὰς μεθοδείας τοῦ διαβόλου· τὴν δὲ τῶν αἱρετικῶν κακόνοιαν ἐθαυμάσαμεν, θεωροῦντες πῶς τοσοῦτον εἰς ἀσεβείας βάραθρον πεπτώκασιν, ὡς μηκέτι μηδὲ τὰς αἰσθήσεις σώζειν, ἀλλὰ πανταχόθεν διεφθαρμένην ἔχειν τὴν διάνοιαν. Τοῦτο δὲ τὸ ἐπιχείρημα διαβόλου μέν ἐστιν ὑποβολὴ, τῶν δὲ παρανόμων Ἰου δαίων μίμησις. Ὥσπερ γὰρ ἐκεῖνοι, πανταχόθεν ἐλεγχόμενοι, προφάσεις ἐπενόουν καθ' ἑαυτῶν, ἵνα μόνον τὸν Κύριον ἀρνήσωνται, καὶ τὰ προφητευθέντα καθ' ἑαυτῶν ἐπισπάσωνται· τὸν αὐτὸν τρόπον καὶ οὗτοι, θεωροῦντες ἑαυτοὺς πανταχόθεν στηλιτευομένους, καὶ βλέποντες γενομένην βδελυκτὴν παρὰ πᾶσι τὴν αἵρεσιν αὐτῶν, ἐφευρεταὶ γίνονται κακῶν, ἵνα μὴ, παυόμενοι ταῖς πρὸς τὴν ἀλήθειαν μάχαις, ἀληθῶς Χριστομάχοι διαμείνωσι. Πόθεν γὰρ αὐτοῖς ἀνέδυ καὶ τοῦτο τὸ κακόν; Πῶς ὅλως τετολμήκασι τὴν καινὴν ταύτην δυσφημίαν φθέγξασθαι κατὰ τοῦ Σωτῆρος; ἀλλ', ὡς ἔοικε, πονηρὸν ὁ ἀσεβὴς, καὶ ἀδόκιμος ὄντως περὶ τὴν πίστιν. Πρότερον γὰρ, ἀρνούμενοι τὴν θεότητα τοῦ μονογενοῦς Υἱοῦ τοῦ Θεοῦ, ὑπεκρίνοντο κἂν τὴν ἔνσαρκον αὐτοῦ παρουσίαν ἐπι γινώσκειν· νῦν δὲ, κατ' ὀλίγον ὑποκαταβαίνοντες, ἐξέπεσαν καὶ ταύτης αὐτῶν τῆς οἰήσεως, καὶ παντα χόθεν ἄθεοι γεγόνασιν, ὥστε μήτε Θεὸν αὐτὸν ἐπιγινώσκειν, μήθ' ὅτι ἄνθρωπος γέγονε πιστεύειν. Εἰ γὰρ ἐπίστευον, οὐκ ἂν τοιαῦτα ἐφθέγξαντο, οἷα ἔγραψεν ἡ σὴ θεοσέβεια κατ' αὐτῶν. Σὺ μὲν οὖν, ἀγαπητὲ καὶ ἀληθῶς ποθεινό τατε, πρέποντα τῇ ἐκκλησιαστικῇ παραδόσει καὶ τῇ εἰς τὸν Κύριον εὐσεβείᾳ πεποίηκας, ἐλέγξας, καὶ παραινέσας καὶ ἐπιτιμήσας τοῖς τοιούτοις· ἐπειδὴ δὲ, παροξυνόμενοι παρὰ τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτῶν τοῦ δια βόλου, οὐκ ἔγνωσαν, οὐδὲ συνῆκαν, κατὰ τὸ γεγραμμένον, ἀλλὰ ἐν σκότει διαπορεύονται· μανθανέτωσαν παρὰ τῆς σῆς εὐλαβείας, ὡς ἡ τοιαύτη αὐτῶν κακόνοια Οὐαλεντίνου καὶ Μαρκίωνος καὶ Μανιχαίου ἐστίν· ὧν οἱ μὲν ἀντὶ ἀληθείας δόκησιν εἰσηγήσαντο, οἱ δὲ διαιροῦντες τὰ ἀδιαίρετα ἠρνήσαντο τὸ, Ὁ Λόγος σὰρξ ἐγένετο, καὶ ἐσκήνωσεν ἐν ἡμῖν. Διὰ τί οὖν, τὰ τούτων φρονοῦντες, οὐχὶ καὶ τῶν ὀνομάτων αὐτῶν γίνονται κληρονόμοι; Εὔλογον γὰρ ὧν τὴν κακοδοξίαν ἔχουσι, τούτων ἔχειν καὶ τὰ ὀνόματα, ἵνα λοιπὸν Οὐαλεντινιανοὶ καὶ Μαρκιωνισταὶ καὶ Μανιχαῖοι καλῶνται. Τάχα κἂν οὕτως διὰ τὴν τῶν ὀνομάτων δυσωδίαν αἰσχυνόμενοι κατανοῆσαι δυνηθῶσιν, εἰς ὅσον βάθος ἀσεβείας πεπτώκασι. Καὶ ἦν μὲν δίκαιον μηκέτι τούτοις ἀποκρί νασθαι, κατὰ τὴν παραίνεσιν τὴν ἀποστολικήν· Αἱρετικὸν ἄνθρωπον μετὰ μίαν καὶ δευτέραν νου θεσίαν παραιτοῦ, εἰδὼς, ὅτι ἐξέστραπται ὁ τοιοῦ τος, καὶ ἁμαρτάνει ὢν αὐτοκατάκριτος· μάλιστα ὅτι καὶ ὁ προφήτης περὶ τῶν τοιούτων φησίν· Ὁ μωρὸς μωρὰ λαλήσει, καὶ ἡ καρδία αὐτοῦ μάταια νοήσει· ἐπειδὴ δὲ κατὰ τὸν ἡγούμενον αὐ τῶν περιέρχονται καὶ αὐτοὶ, ὡς λέοντες, ζητοῦντες τίνα καταπίωσι τῶν ἀκεραίων· τούτου ἕνεκεν ἀναγκαῖον γέγονεν ἡμῖν τῇ σῇ εὐλαβείᾳ ἀντιγράψαι, ἵνα, πάλιν διὰ τῆς σῆς νουθεσίας μαθόντες οἱ ἀδελφοὶ, καταγινώσκωσιν ἐπὶ πλεῖον τῆς ἐκείνων ματαιολογίας.
thought_title: Praise for Adelphius and diagnosis of the Arians' new blasphemy
orientation: Athanasius opens his letter to Bishop Adelphius, praising his piety and condemning the Arians' latest denial of the incarnation.
pass_a_gloss: Of our father among the saints Athanasius, archbishop of Alexandria, letter to Adelphius bishop and confessor, against the Arians. Having encountered the things written by your piety, we truly welcomed your piety toward Christ, and we glorified God especially, who gave you such grace, so that you both have right understanding and do not fail to know as far as possible the schemes of the devil; but we marveled at the evil mind of the heretics, seeing how they have fallen into such a depth of impiety, as no longer even to preserve their senses, but to have their mind corrupted from every side. This attempt is a suggestion of the devil, and an imitation of the lawless Jews. For just as those men, being refuted from every side, devised pretexts against themselves, in order only to deny the Lord, and to draw upon themselves the things prophesied against themselves; in the same way these men too, seeing themselves branded from every side, and seeing their heresy become abominable among all, become inventors of evils, in order that, not ceasing from their battles against the truth, they may truly remain fighters against Christ. For whence did this evil arise for them? How at all have they dared to utter this new blasphemy against the Savior? But, as it seems, the impious man is wicked, and truly worthless concerning the faith. For formerly, denying the divinity of the only-begotten Son of God, they pretended at least to recognize his incarnate presence; but now, descending little by little, they have fallen away even from this opinion of theirs, and have become godless from every side, so as neither to recognize him as God, nor to believe that he became man. For if they believed, they would not have uttered such things as your piety wrote against them. You therefore, beloved and truly most longed-for, have done what is fitting to the church tradition and to piety toward the Lord, having refuted, and admonished, and rebuked such men; but since, being provoked by their father the devil, they did not know, nor did they understand, according to what is written, but they walk in darkness; let them learn from your reverence that such evil mind of theirs is of Valentinus and Marcion and Mani; of whom some introduced mere appearance instead of truth, and others, dividing the things that cannot be divided, denied the saying, The Word became flesh, and dwelt among us. Why then, thinking the things of these men, do they not also become heirs of their names? For it is reasonable that those whose evil opinion they have, of these they should also have the names, so that henceforth they may be called Valentinians and Marcionites and Manichaeans. Perhaps even so, being ashamed because of the stench of the names, they may be able to perceive into what depth of impiety they have fallen. And it was just no longer to answer these men, according to the apostolic admonition: Reject a heretical man after a first and second admonition, knowing that such a man has been turned aside and sins, being self-condemned; especially because the prophet also says about such men: The fool will speak foolish things, and his heart will think vain things; but since, according to their leader, they too go around like lions, seeking whom they may swallow of the innocent; for this reason it has become necessary for us to write back to your reverence, so that, again learning through your admonition, the brothers may condemn more fully the empty talk of those men.

pass_b_english: We read what your piety wrote, and we truly welcomed your reverence for Christ. Above all we glorified God, who gave you such grace that you both hold sound understanding and are not ignorant, as far as possible, of the devil's schemes. But we marveled at the heretics' malice, seeing how far they have fallen into the pit of impiety, so that they no longer even keep their senses but have their minds corrupted on every side. This attempt of theirs is a prompting of the devil and an imitation of the lawless Jews. For just as those men, refuted on every side, kept inventing pretexts against themselves, only so that they might deny the Lord and bring upon themselves what had been prophesied against them, in the same way these men, seeing themselves publicly denounced on every side and seeing their heresy become abominable to all, become inventors of evils, so that they may not stop fighting against the truth but may truly remain fighters against Christ. For where did this evil of theirs spring from? How have they dared at all to utter this new blasphemy against the Savior? But, as it seems, the impious man is wicked and truly worthless in matters of faith. For earlier, while denying the divinity of the only-begotten Son of God, they pretended at least to acknowledge his incarnate presence. But now, descending little by little, they have fallen away even from this opinion of theirs and have become godless on every side, so that they neither acknowledge him as God nor believe that he became a human being. For if they believed, they would not have uttered the sorts of things your piety wrote against them. You then, beloved and truly longed-for one, have done what befits the Church's tradition and reverence for the Lord, by refuting, admonishing, and rebuking such men. But since, provoked by their father the devil, they did not know or understand, as it is written, but walk in darkness, let them learn from your reverence that this malice of theirs belongs to Valentinus, Marcion, and Mani. Of these, some introduced mere appearance in place of truth, while others, dividing the things that cannot be divided, denied that "The Word became flesh and dwelt among us" (John 1:14). Why then, since they think the thoughts of those men, do they not also inherit their names? For it is reasonable that those who hold their evil doctrine should also bear their names, so that from now on they may be called Valentinians, Marcionites, and Manichaeans. Perhaps then, ashamed by the stench of the names, they may be able to understand into what depth of impiety they have fallen. It would have been right to answer them no longer, according to the apostolic counsel: "Reject a divisive person after a first and second warning, knowing that such a person is twisted and sins, being self-condemned" (Titus 3:10-11); especially since the prophet also says about such people: "The fool will speak folly, and his heart will devise vain things" (Isaiah 32:6). But since, like their leader, they too go around like lions seeking someone to devour among the innocent, for this reason it has become necessary for us to write back to your reverence, so that the brothers, learning again through your admonition, may condemn their empty talk even more.
